protections: A custom generator call must return instead of spinning when its resolved ID size cannot be reached: the size default is applied first and the non-positive/non-numeric/non-finite decision is taken inside the returned closure before `while (true)` (index.js:53-65, index.browser.js:36-47).

Every shipped implementation of that generator carries the decision: Node ESM (index.js:33-66), the browser/react-native ESM copy (index.browser.js:12-49) and the documented non-secure alternative (non-secure/index.js:12-34).

The generation loop can make progress on its own: the step and mask derived at factory time (index.js:38, index.js:51, index.browser.js:18, index.browser.js:34) are finite and positive for the alphabet and default supplied.

The size shapes the suite already accepts keep working: an omitted size defaults (index.js:53, index.js:68), string and fractional sizes are accepted (test/index.test.js:47-49, test/index.test.js:60-65, test/index.test.js:129-136), and custom getRandom byte consumption is unchanged (test/index.test.js:147-150).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: index.browser.js is selected only by the browser and react-native export conditions (package.json:35, package.json:36, package.json:42, package.json:45), so a Node-side reproduction of the reported hang looks complete without it.

nanoid/non-secure is documented as the explicitly insecure alternative (README.md:232-241) and its loop needs a negative size because size 0 already yields '' (non-secure/index.js:16-17), while the report's trigger is a zero size in the secure generator.

the advisory names custom generators; nanoid(size) is a different entry point, and the secure Node nanoid() converts its size with |= 0 (index.js:74) and yields an empty string for a negative size instead of looping, so this loop looks unaffected.

NaN and undefined are not zero or negative integers, and the reported input shape was a zero or negative integer; the obvious `size <= 0` guard does not fire on them, nor on a non-numeric string size.

alphabet validity is presented as the caller's precondition ('Alphabet must contain 256 symbols or less', index.d.ts:33, README.md:265), and an empty alphabet is not a size at all, so the reported input shape does not reach it.

the reported case is a zero default with no argument; calling the returned generator with an explicit positive size looks like a valid call, and the exit test at index.js:62 compares the positive size, so the zero step produced at index.js:51 is never inspected.

the defaulted call works today (customAlphabet('a', 5)() returns 'aaaaa'), so nothing looks wrong; but the effective size is produced by the closure default `size = defaultSize` (index.js:53) from the factory default `size = 21` (index.js:68), so a guard written on the raw argument or at the customAlphabet boundary either misses the no-argument hang or returns '' for every defaulted call.

the CLI already rejects NaN and non-positive sizes (bin/nanoid.js:38, test/bin.test.js:42-47), and Number('1e999') === Infinity is a numeric-syntax curiosity that passes the positivity test, so the size validation looks done.

masking: index.browser.js:34 rounds with `-~`, so a zero factory default produces step 1 there: the reported zero-size case terminates in the browser copy while a negative or NaN default still spins (index.browser.js:34, index.browser.js:42, index.browser.js:45), hiding the missing guard in the second implementation.

Once a `size <= 0` guard exists in index.js:53, T7 (a non-positive factory default with an explicit positive call size, step 0 at index.js:51) is the only remaining spin in the same closure, and the guard's presence makes that closure look protected.

conflicts.what: The natural predicate for T5 is stricter size validation, but Number.isInteger(size) or typeof size === 'number' refuses the string size that nanoid('10') pins (test/index.test.js:47-49) and the fractional sizes pinned at test/index.test.js:60-65 and test/index.test.js:129-136, while a guard on the raw closure argument before the `= defaultSize` default (index.js:53) turns every defaulted call into '' instead of 'aaaaa' (test/index.test.js:92-95).

The published contract changes at the same line: customAlphabet('a', 5)(0) returns a one-character ID today and must become '', so a guard placed at the customAlphabet boundary rather than inside the closure either leaves per-call sizes unguarded or returns '' for the defaulted call that test/index.test.js:92-95 pins.

fairness_risks: String sizes are legitimate and tested: nanoid('10') must stay 10 characters (test/index.test.js:47-49) and the CLI converts argv with Number (bin/nanoid.js:36); a rule that accepts only a primitive number refuses a pinned shape.

Fractional sizes are legitimate and tested: nanoid(2.1) and customAlphabet(ALPHABET)(2.1) must not hang or pollute the pool (test/index.test.js:60-65, test/index.test.js:129-136); a rule demanding a positive integer refuses them.
A single-symbol alphabet is legitimate and tested: customAlphabet('a', 5)() must return 'aaaaa' (test/index.test.js:92-95, test/non-secure.test.js:67-70); any alphabet-length floor above 1 breaks it.

The package's own answer for an invalid size is '' rather than an exception: non-secure size 0 already returns '' through `while (i--)` (non-secure/index.js:16-17), so a RangeError rule contradicts existing behaviour and any hidden test derived from the fix.
customRandom's supplied getRandom must keep consuming exactly step bytes: test/index.test.js:147-150 pins 'adca' and 'cbadcbadcbadcbadcc'; a guard that consumes bytes before returning changes them.

bin/nanoid.js:49-50 passes an undefined size to customAlphabet when --alphabet is used without --size, relying on the `= 21` default at index.js:68 even though README.md:416 calls --size required; refusing undefined at the customAlphabet boundary breaks that accepted invocation.

design.why: Four independent groups over three shipped modules. G1 {T1,T5,T8,T9}: decide on the resolved size inside the Node closure with a predicate covering 0, negatives, NaN/undefined and Infinity while keeping the `= defaultSize` default and the pinned string/fractional sizes. G2 {T2}: the same decision in the browser/react-native implementation, whose different step arithmetic (index.browser.js:34, index.browser.js:41) makes the zero case pass while negatives and NaN still spin. G3 {T3,T4}: the documented non-secure module, where size 0 already returns '' so only a negative size hangs, in two separate loops. G4 {T6,T7}: progress that does not depend on the caller's size - an empty alphabet (mask -1 at index.js:38, step -Infinity at index.js:51) and a non-positive factory default with an explicit positive call size (step 0 at index.js:51 while index.js:62 tests the positive size). This beats a three-group design because G2 and G3 are pure discovery traps with real dismissal arguments (export condition; documented insecure alternative), G4 is the only one that forces reasoning about the factory-time step rather than the size argument (a zero-step producer the size check never sees), and G1 is where an over-strict fix breaks the pinned defaulted, string and fractional calls - the coupled-value failure MiMo is prone to. Different reasons to dismiss per group: none/surface for G1, browser condition for G2, insecure module plus negative-only trigger for G3, caller precondition plus a seemingly valid positive call for G4. Caveat: only G1 and G2 correspond to behaviour the published fix changes in this tree; G3 and G4 are uncovered_upstream routes and need hidden tests authored to the '' contract, not replayed from the upstream diff.
